plain_what: A feed-forward layer needs a gate that decides how much of a signal passes. Here the gate signal becomes a unit rotation, and the signal is rotated by it, four numbers at a time. A rotation only turns a vector and needs no exponential or squashing curve. The old gate used a sigmoid, which the rules now ban.
how_it_works: Work on 4-lane blocks. Let g be a gate block and u the matching up (value) block of the MLP hidden layer. Compute r = sqrt(|g|^2 + 1e-12) and q = g / r, a unit quaternion, then out = q (x) u, the Hamilton product. This is a rotation of R4, so |out| = |u| whenever q is a unit quaternion; a zero gate block gives q = 0 and out = 0. Backward (exact, with the normalisation Jacobian): du = conj(q) (x) d, dq = d (x) conj(u), dg = (dq - q (q . dq)) / r. No exp, sigmoid, tanh or softmax appears in either direction. The hidden width must be divisible by 4. One CUDA thread handles one 4-block (hamilton_gate_fwd/bwd, shared source for f32 and bf16). The config field Gate defaults to Swiglu (the sigmoid gate, kept so old artifacts load byte-identically); Hamilton is selected with gate=hamilton, and export/D11 and qat refuse any non-default gate. The same op is the output gate of the geometric recurrence. Still open by the owner's card: an icosian snap of q (so the product becomes a Cayley-table read), an exact hard forward with a straight-through bridge, a serving form, and a named hazard that a near-zero gate block makes dg about 1/r = 1e6.
geometry: Unit quaternions (S3) and the Hamilton product acting on R4 blocks; the planned icosian snap would use the 120 unit icosians (600-cell) and the 120x120 Cayley table.

rule_compat.D11: Not servable today: the exporter refuses any gate other than swiglu, and the normalisation divides by a square root and multiplies two runtime values. It becomes table-servable only after the icosian snap makes q one of 120 icosians, so q (x) u is a Cayley-table read plus shifts.
rule_compat.D23: Passes by construction: no exp, sigmoid, tanh, softplus or softmax in forward or backward. D25 closed the SwiGLU sigmoid exception, which this replaces.
rule_compat.D30: A per-4-block Hamilton product, not a dense contraction and not GEMM; the owner permits a geometric feed-forward block (Hamilton gate plus Hamilton projections). The dense projection half of that block has since been retired in favour of SpiralCore/FBS.
rule_compat.D32_D37: A float op, frozen by D32 section 4; D37 section 5 lets it return only by re-registration. The earlier G1 rectified-square arm was withdrawn by the owner as non-geometric and no G1 source ships.

open_questions: Does a rotation gate express enough? An amplitude gate (SwiGLU) can shut a channel; a unit rotation cannot.
How is q snapped to one of 120 icosians without losing the cost advantage seen for weights (+0.0196 BPB for exact activations in the activation-snap study)?
Is the geometric feed-forward block (Hamilton gate plus structured projections) worth building once the dense projection half is retired?
Does it add anything over the discrete model's own gating (ternary trits), or does a float gate over a discrete carrier duplicate the same question at higher cost (architect audit, 18 Oct)?

figure_ideas: A value vector drawn as an arrow in 3D (a 4D quaternion block projected down). Sweep the gate input: under a sigmoid gate the arrow shrinks to nothing; under the Hamilton gate it keeps its length and swings around the sphere. Shows what the replacement does and does not do.

Two feed-forward block wiring diagrams side by side: SwiGLU (gate -> sigmoid -> times up) and Hamilton (gate -> divide by length -> quaternion product with up), with the banned operation crossed out and the table-read replacement for the product shown as a dashed future box.
